question: When does the third stage of labor officially begin?

options.A: After the complete delivery of the baby
options.B: When the mother feels the urge to push
options.C: At the start of full cervical dilation
options.D: When the placenta starts to separate

explanation: The third stage starts right after the baby is fully born and ends when the placenta and membranes come out. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T4#BMP212_U3_T4_h1)

question: What makes the third stage of labor a time that requires close watch by the midwife?

options.A: There is a high risk of heavy bleeding
options.B: Infection rates peak immediately after birth
options.C: The mother is too exhausted to breathe well
options.D: The cervix usually tears during this time

explanation: Because the placental site leaves open blood vessels, postpartum hemorrhage is the main danger during this brief stage. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T4#BMP212_U3_T4_h1)

question: Which placental separation pattern begins at the center and looks like an inverted umbrella upon delivery?
explanation: The Schultze mechanism starts centrally, forming a clot that turns the placenta inside out as it exits. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T4#BMP212_U3_T4_h2)

question: What causes the placenta to peel away from the uterine wall right after the baby is born?

options.A: The sudden rush of amniotic fluid pushing it down
options.B: The continuous pumping action of the fetal heart
options.C: The forceful pulling of the umbilical cord by the attendant
options.D: The sudden reduction in the surface area of the uterus

explanation: When the uterus shrinks rapidly after birth, the rigid placenta cannot shrink with it, causing it to tear away. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T4#BMP212_U3_T4_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT a sign that the placenta has separated?

options.B: A sudden gush of dark blood from the vagina
options.C: Lengthening of the visible umbilical cord
options.D: The uterus changing to a globular shape

explanation: Severe continuous pain is a sign of complications like abruption or rupture, not normal physiological placental separation. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T4#BMP212_U3_T4_h3)

question: A midwife notices that the umbilical cord hanging from the vagina has suddenly grown longer and the uterus is globular. What do these signs tell her?

options.B: The placenta has separated and moved down
options.C: The baby has not been fully delivered yet
options.D: A postpartum hemorrhage has already begun

explanation: Cord lengthening and a globular uterine shape are classic indicators that the placenta has detached and descended. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T4#BMP212_U3_T4_h3)

question: What main body action stops bleeding from the open vessels where the placenta was attached?

options.A: Rapid activation of systemic platelets and clotting factors
options.B: Natural cooling of the uterus from amniotic fluid loss
options.C: Contraction of crisscrossing myometrial muscle fibers
options.D: Pressure from the baby pressing on the cervix

explanation: The myometrium acts as living ligatures, squeezing the blood vessels shut to control bleeding after birth. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T4#BMP212_U3_T4_h4)

question: Why are blood clotting factors alone not enough to stop bleeding in the third stage of labor?

options.A: Pregnancy temporarily destroys all circulating clotting proteins
options.B: Clotting only works in arteries, not in the venous sinuses
options.C: The placenta prevents any clotting from happening inside the uterus
options.D: The vessels feeding the placenta are large and require muscular compression to close

explanation: Blood clots alone cannot withstand the high flow from large uterine vessels without the mechanical clamping of muscle fibers. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T4#BMP212_U3_T4_h4)

question: What defines the physiological method of placental expulsion?

options.A: Applying steady downward traction on the cord without waiting
options.B: Using manual removal of the placenta under regional anesthesia
options.C: Using natural maternal effort and gravity without drugs or pulling
options.D: Injecting oxytocin immediately after the baby's shoulder is born

explanation: Physiological management lets the body expel the placenta completely on its own without medical or physical interference. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T4#BMP212_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is the main benefit of active management of the third stage compared to physiological management?

options.A: It entirely eliminates the need for any midwife supervision
options.B: It significantly reduces the risk of postpartum hemorrhage
options.C: It prevents all perineal tears from occurring
options.D: It makes the delivery of the baby happen much faster

explanation: Active management uses uterotonics and controlled traction to shorten the third stage and lower blood loss. [learn more](BMP212_U3_T4#BMP212_U3_T4_h5)
